articles.title: Reino Unido vai compartilhar arma secreta com a Ucrânia | G1
articles.standfirst: Autorização para produção de mísseis permitirá a criação de linhas de montagem em território ucraniano, mas produção deve levar anos.
articles.summary: Autorização para produção de mísseis permitirá a criação de linhas de montagem em território ucraniano, mas produção deve levar anos.
articles.body:
Míssil de cruzeiro Storm Shadow, fabricado pelo Reino Unido. — Foto: AP Photo/Lewis Joly, File

O Reino Unido deve dar acesso à Ucrânia ao sistema de mísseis Storm Shadow (Sombra da tempestade, em tradução livre), desenvolvidos em parceria com a França . A medida, anunciada nesta segunda-feira (24) pelo primeiro-ministro Andy Burnham , permitirá que os ucranianos produzam as armas no próprio país .

🔎O Storm Shadow, como o míssil é chamado no Reino Unido, e o SCALP, nome usado pela França, são versões da mesma arma, desenvolvida pela fabricante europeia MBDA.

✅ Siga o canal de notícias internacionais do g1 no WhatsApp

A Ucrânia já utiliza os dois mísseis contra alvos militares russos. Eles são lançados por aviões de combate e usados principalmente contra instalações protegidas, como bunkers e centros de comando.

A transferência de tecnologia, porém, não deve mudar o rumo da guerra de imediato. A produção de um míssil desse é cara - cerca de 1 milhão de libras (R$ 7,02 milhões) -, e exige uma cadeia de fornecedores que ainda precisará ser estruturada em território ucraniano.

Especialistas avaliam que pode levar anos até que a produção local alcance uma escala relevante. A familiaridade da Ucrânia com o Storm Shadow e o SCALP pode acelerar o processo, mas não elimina os desafios industriais.

Rússia quer aumentar produção de mísseis e recrutar 300 mil novos soldados para guerra na Ucrânia, afirma Zelensky

Coreia do Norte lança mísseis balísticos em meio a exercícios conjuntos de EUA e Coreia do Sul

EUA estão vulneráveis? Como a baixa nos estoques de mísseis ameaça a defesa norte-americana

A dificuldade expõe um problema mais amplo enfrentado pelos países ocidentais. Reino Unido e outros integrantes da Otan passaram décadas investindo em armas de alta tecnologia, mas produzidas em quantidades relativamente pequenas. Em uma guerra longa, os estoques podem acabar rapidamente.

O próprio Reino Unido mudou sua estratégia. O país deixou de comprar novos Storm Shadow e passou a desenvolver um novo míssil de longo alcance, o Brakestop, com menos dependência de componentes estrangeiros e custo inferior ao da arma franco-britânica.

A Ucrânia, por outro lado, ampliou rapidamente sua indústria militar durante a guerra. O país passou a produzir drones e outros armamentos em grande escala, usando em alguns casos componentes comerciais de baixo custo. Os drones de longo alcance se tornaram uma das principais formas de Kiev atacar instalações russas a centenas de quilômetros da fronteira.

Esse avanço, porém, não resolve todos os problemas. A Ucrânia ainda depende de países aliados para armas mais complexas, principalmente sistemas capazes de interceptar mísseis balísticos russos.

O exemplo mais urgente é o Patriot , fabricado nos Estados Unidos . A escassez de interceptadores tem deixado parte da defesa aérea ucraniana vulnerável às ondas de ataques russos. Em agosto, o presidente Volodymyr Zelensky disse que as entregas de interceptadores em 2026 haviam caído para cerca de um terço do volume recebido no ano anterior.

A falta de Patriots também se agravou por causa da demanda gerada por outros conflitos. A Ucrânia pediu autorização para fabricar os interceptadores em seu território, mas o governo de Donald Trump recuou de um apoio inicial à ideia.

Enquanto isso, empresas ucranianas tentam desenvolver alternativas próprias. A Fire Point, por exemplo, produz mísseis de cruzeiro e drones capazes de atingir alvos a longa distância dentro da Rússia.

A Ucrânia também trabalha no desenvolvimento de interceptadores próprios, com apoio europeu. O desafio é maior: destruir um míssil em alta velocidade exige tecnologia muito mais complexa do que a empregada em drones de ataque.

A iniciativa também provocou reação da Rússia. O Kremlin acusou o Reino Unido de aumentar seu envolvimento no conflito e afirmou que o compartilhamento de tecnologia representa uma escalada da participação britânica na guerra.

A visita de Burnham acontece no mesmo dia em que a União Europeia anunciou um novo pacote de ajuda de € 6,1 bilhões (R$ 36 bilhões) para a Ucrânia. O dinheiro faz parte de um empréstimo de € 90 bilhões concedido ao país.

Segundo a Comissão Europeia, o reforço militar é cada vez mais urgente diante dos ataques russos. Em julho, a Rússia lançou quase 400 mísseis contra a Ucrânia.

Mais da metade dos recursos será destinada à área militar. O objetivo é reforçar a defesa aérea da Ucrânia e aumentar a disponibilidade de mísseis e munições. Entre as principais necessidades estão os interceptadores Patriot.

O anúncio ocorreu no mesmo dia em que a Ucrânia celebra 35 anos de independência. Zelensky se reuniu nesta segunda com líderes europeus que integram a chamada Coalizão dos Dispostos. A presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen , declarou apoio ao país e afirmou que a UE mantém seu compromisso com os ucranianos.

articles.title: Trump quer oficializar US$ 100 mil para vistos de alta qualificação  | G1
articles.standfirst: Casa Branca divulgou proposta para elevar a taxa para a concessão do visto H-1B, para trabalhadores altamente qualificados. Valor é o mais alto já cobrado para a emissão de um visto nos EUA.Trump alega que empresas deixam de contratar cidadãos nacionais. Índia e China lideram ranking do H-1B.
articles.summary: O governo dos EUA quer tornar permanente a taxa de mais de US$ 103.265 (cerca de R$ 531 mil) sobre novos vistos do tipo H-1B,  de trabalhadores altamente qualificados.
articles.body:
Imagem de visto dos Estados Unidos. — Foto: Divulgação

O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , quer estabelecer de forma permanente uma taxa sem precedentes para a concessão de vistos H-1B, de alta qualificação, nos Estados Unidos.

Nesta segunda-feira (24), o governo Trump divulgou uma proposta de regulamentação para oficializar uma taxa de mais de US$ 103.265 (cerca de R$ 531 mil) sobre novos vistos do tipo H-1B, destinados a trabalhadores estrangeiros altamente qualificados. Atualmente, o custo para esse visto variam de US$ 2.000 a US$ 5.000.

✅ Siga o canal de notícias internacionais do g1 no WhatsApp

➡️Embora sua política anti-imigratória foque em imigrantes em situação irregular nos EUA, Donald Trump é um crítico do programa H-1B . Ele argumenta que empresas o utilizam para substituir trabalhadores norte-americanos por mão de obra estrangeira mais barata. Mas diversas empresas afirmam que H-1B supre a escassez de trabalhadores qualificados .

A taxa de US$ 100 mil já havia sido imposta por Trump no ano passado, mas a Justiça dos EUA proibiu a cobrança, apontando ilegaldidade . A Casa Branca apresentou um recurso, que vem sendo analisado por um tribunal de apelações.

Mas Trump instituiu a taxa invocando o poder presidencial previsto na legislação federal de imigração para restringir a entrada de certos cidadãos estrangeiros cuja presença seria prejudicial aos interesses dos EUA.

Com isso, ele determinou que o Departamento de Segurança Interna dos EUA adotasse regulamentações para tornar a taxa permanente . A estimativa é que a norma poderá ser formalizada até o final do ano .

O H-1B é utilizado, principalmente, pelos setores de tecnologia, educação e pesquisa nos EUA. Índia e China são os países das principais nacionalidades contratadas por empresas norte-americanas com esse tipo de visto, segundo a plataforma de dados Visual Capitalist e Statista. O Brasil aparece em 9º lugar da lista.

👉 O programa H-1B permite que empregadores dos EUA contratem trabalhadores estrangeiros com formação em áreas especializadas e oferece 65.000 vistos anualmente , além de outros 20.000 para trabalhadores com diplomas de pós-graduação (mestrado ou doutorado), com validade de três a seis anos.

Até o final de fevereiro deste ano, cerca de 70 empregadores haviam pago a taxa de US$ 100.000, segundo documentos judiciais.

A taxa também está sendo contestada pela Câmara de Comércio dos EUA — o maior grupo de lobby empresarial do país —, por estados governados por democratas e por uma coalizão de sindicatos e empregadores. Essas ações judiciais poderão ser alteradas para contestar a norma proposta nesta semana, assim que ela for oficializada.

O presidente Donald Trump conversa com repórteres após chegar a bordo do Air Force One na terça-feira, 11 de agosto de 2026, na Base Aérea Conjunta Andrews, em Maryland — Foto: Mark Schiefelbein

As ações judiciais alegam que o poder de Trump de restringir a entrada de estrangeiros não lhe confere autoridade para se sobrepor à lei que criou o programa de vistos H-1B. Os estados e grupos autores das ações também afirmam que o Departamento de Segurança Interna não pode impor taxas, impostos ou outros meios de gerar receita para os Estados Unidos sem a autorização do Congresso .

O governo Trump sustenta que a taxa não constitui um imposto tradicional e que os tribunais têm pouca margem para questionar a autoridade do presidente em restringir a entrada de pessoas no país.

Em meio às medidas mais amplas de restrição à imigração adotadas por Trump, empresas dos EUA solicitaram cerca de 344.000 vistos H-1B no ano passado — uma queda de mais de 25% em relação a 2024 e menos da metade dos 794.000 vistos solicitados em 2023, segundo dados do Serviço de Cidadania e Imigração dos EUA (USCIS).

O governo Trump também determinou uma análise mais rigorosa dos candidatos ao visto H-1B e propôs um novo processo de seleção que privilegiaria trabalhadores mais qualificados e com salários mais altos.

No início de agosto, em uma norma separada, o Departamento de Segurança Interna estabeleceu taxas de até US$ 4.500 (R$ cerca de 23 mil) para solicitações de extensão de permanência de trabalhadores com visto H-1B ou para a transferência de funcionários sediados em outros países para os Estados Unidos.

articles.title: Príncipe Harry deixa ONG africana envolvida em escândalo | G1
articles.standfirst: Organização African Parks foi alvo de denúncias de abusos contra moradores locais por parte de alguns de seus guardas florestais em um parque nacional da República do Congo.
articles.summary: Organização African Parks foi alvo de denúncias de abusos contra moradores locais por parte de alguns de seus guardas florestais em um parque nacional da República do Congo.
articles.body:
O príncipe britânico Harry comparece a tribunal no Reino Unido, em 9 de abril de 2025. — Foto: Reuters/Isabel Infantes

O príncipe Harry deixou o seu posto na direção de uma organização não governamental dedicada à preservação da natureza no continente africano, após denúncias de abusos contra moradores locais por parte de alguns de seus guardas florestais , confirmou nesta segunda-feira (24) o porta-voz do membro da realeza.

✅ Siga o canal de notícias internacionais do g1 no WhatsApp

Harry não faz mais parte do conselho administrativo da African Parks, que em maio de 2025 reconheceu que seus guardas florestais participaram de "abusos" em um parque nacional da República do Congo, na África Central.

Informações publicadas pelo jornal britânico "Mail on Sunday" e pelo programa alemão "Tagesschau" repercutiram as denúncias de moradores locais, que relataram estupros, espancamentos, torturas e outros abusos cometidos por guardas florestais contratados pela African Parks, no Parque Nacional de Odzala-Kokoua, no norte do Congo.

A organização beneficente confirmou no ano passado que uma investigação independente havia corroborado as denúncias. No entanto, não forneceu detalhes sobre os estupros cometidos contra a comunidade baka, que vive nas proximidades do parque.

Segundo o relatório do órgão independente, as acusações contra os guardas florestais contratados pela African Parks - que administra 24 áreas protegidas em 13 países e recebeu financiamento da União Europeia e dos Estados Unidos - incluíam estupros e torturas.

Harry declarou que estava "orgulhoso de seus dez anos na African Parks e apoia plenamente o processo em curso para reforçar seu conselho de administração. Seu compromisso com a conservação na África permanece e ele continua apoiando a missão", segundo um comunicado de seu porta-voz.

A ONG afirmou, por sua vez, que o príncipe e o conselho de administração "concordaram mutuamente que, após dez anos de serviço, este era o momento adequado para que ele encerrasse sua função oficial, como parte de uma renovação rotineira da estrutura" interna.

articles.title: Presidente da Colômbia ordena deportações de migrantes em situação irregular | G1
articles.standfirst: País foi o que mais recebeu imigrantes venezuelanos na última década.
articles.summary: País foi o que mais recebeu imigrantes venezuelanos na última década.
articles.body:
O presidente da Colômbia, Abelardo de la Espriella , ordenou nesta segunda-feira (24) a deportação de imigrantes irregulares do país e determinou a coordenação entre a autoridade migratória e a polícia.

Segundo um vídeo vazado de um conselho de segurança, realizado no domingo (23), em Barranquilla, no norte do país, o mandatário deu instruções pra identificar e deter primeiro os migrantes que cometeram crimes.

✅ Siga o canal de notícias internacionais do g1 no WhatsApp

"A ordem à Imigração é clara (....) Primeiro, os que estão cometendo crimes, segundo os que não têm sua situação regularizada e que, no curto prazo, terão que ser deportados", disse ele.

"Não vou aceitar a imigração ilegal. Primeiro, os colombianos, segundo os colombianos e terceiro os colombianos, para que fique claro para todo mundo", acrescentou.

Na última década, a Colômbia foi o principal destino de imigrantes venezuelanos que fugiram da crise em seu país.

A Acnur, agência da ONU para os refugiados, estimou que três milhões de venezuelanos vivem na Colômbia em 2025.

Tradicionalmente, a direita colombiana promove políticas de acolhida para a diáspora venezuelana com um forte discurso contra o chavismo.

Casos de abuso sexual de menores explodem entre migrantes em Ceuta

Juíza anula suspensão de vistos imposta por governo Trump a 75 países

O país europeu que endureceu imigração, mas depende de brasileiros para funcionar

"Deportados! É uma ordem presidencial que deve começar a ser cumprida esta mesma semana. Não vou aceitar migrantes ilegais, de onde quer que venham", disse o presidente.

"É uma decisão política e eu a assumo. É uma decisão administrativa e eu a assumo", acrescentou.

Atravessada por seis décadas de conflito armado, a Colômbia não tem tradição de receber migrantes. Por outro lado, milhões de cidadãos do país fugirem da violência e da pobreza para Estados Unidos, Espanha e outros países.

Segundo um vídeo vazado de um conselho de segurança, realizado no domingo (23), em Barranquilla, no norte do país, o mandatário deu instruções pra identificar e deter primeiro os migrantes que cometeram crimes.
✅ Siga o canal de notícias internacionais do g1 no WhatsApp
"A ordem à Imigração é clara (....) Primeiro, os que estão cometendo crimes, segundo os que não têm sua situação regularizada e que, no curto prazo, terão que ser deportados", disse ele.
"Não vou aceitar a imigração ilegal. Primeiro, os colombianos, segundo os colombianos e terceiro os colombianos, para que fique claro para todo mundo", acrescentou.
Na última década, a Colômbia foi o principal destino de imigrantes venezuelanos que fugiram da crise em seu país.
A Acnur, agência da ONU para os refugiados, estimou que três milhões de venezuelanos vivem na Colômbia em 2025.
Tradicionalmente, a direita colombiana promove políticas de acolhida para a diáspora venezuelana com um forte discurso contra o chavismo.

"É uma decisão política e eu a assumo. É uma decisão administrativa e eu a assumo", acrescentou.

articles.title: Governo Trump não descarta usar força militar contra o Irã novamente | G1
articles.standfirst: A declaração é feita num momento em que Washington lança um 'Dia D econômico' contra Teerã e parece deixar de lado os ataques, ao mesmo temporariamente, para sufocar o país do Oriente Médio financeiramente.
articles.summary: A declaração é feita num momento em que Washington lança um 'Dia D econômico' contra Teerã e parece deixar de lado os ataques.
articles.body:
O secretário de Guerra dos EUA, Pete Hegseth, no Panamá em 13 de agosto de 2026 — Foto: Aris Martinez/REUTERS

O Secretário de Defesa dos EUA, Pete Hegseth, afirmou nesta segunda-feira (24) que o governo do presidente Donald Trump não descarta o uso de força militar contra o Irã.

✅ Siga o canal de notícias internacionais do g1 no WhatsApp

A declaração é feita num momento em que Washington lança um "Dia D econômico" contra Teerã e parece deixar de lado os ataques, ao mesmo temporariamente, para sufocar o país do Oriente Médio financeiramente.

"De forma alguma descartamos o uso de ataques cinéticos em qualquer ponto do Estreito de Ormuz ou nos arredores do Irã", disse Hegseth a repórteres, acrescentando que o Irã não conseguiria suportar a pressão econômica a que estava sendo submetido.

Mais cedo nesta segunda, os Estados Unidos anunciaram uma leva de sanções a Teerã, ameaçaram países que realizem transações econômicas com o regime iraniano e lançaram uma campanha para que líderes mundiais rompam com o país persa.

O Departamento do Tesouro norte-americano afirmou ter sancionado cerca de 60 pessoas, entidades e embarcações ligadas governo iraniano e que atuam em áreas de energia nuclear, de produção de mísseis, cibernéticas e de petróleo.

➡️ As sanções fazem parte de uma " guerra econômica" que Trump anunciou na semana passada para tentar sufocar a economia iraniana. Trump já havia dito que esta segunda-feira seria o "Dia D da guerra econômica".

Como parte da estratégia, o governo norte-americano também ameaçou países que fizerem qualquer transação econômica com o Irã. O secretário do Tesouro norte-americano, Scott Bessent, que anunciou as sanções, afirmou que Trump está pedindo para que líderes mundiais cessem relações com o Irã.

O secretário de Tesouro dos Estados Unidos, Scott Bessent, durante anúncio de novo pacote de snações ao Irã, em 24 de agosto de 2026. — Foto: Evelyn Hockstein/ Reuters

O secretário afirmou ainda que Washington definiu um cronograma para que cada país vá interrompendo suas "atividades" com o regime iraniano. "Se eles não interromperem essas atividades, nos faremos isso de forma unilateral através de autoridades do Tesouro", ameaçou Bessent.

Ele disse ainda que uma "grande instituição financeira" também será sancionada nesta semana por vínculos financeiros com o Irã, mas não deu mais detalhes da ameaça.

articles.title: Mega-Sena 3048: aposta que levou R$ 57 milhões foi feita online em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Aposta única de Blumenau levou o prêmio. No estado, outros dois apostadores acertaram a quina e cada um levou R$ 34.212,24.
articles.summary: Aposta única de Blumenau levou o prêmio. No estado, outros dois apostadores saíram vencedores ao acertarem a quina, cada um levou R$34.212,24.
articles.body:
Uma aposta única de Blumenau, em Santa Catarina , foi a vencedora do concurso número 3048 e levou o prêmio de R$ 57.261.598,09. O ganhador realizou a aposta pela internet.

O sorteio foi realizado neste domingo (23), em São Paulo.

📱Favorite o g1 no Google e acompanhe as principais notícias do dia

Clique aqui para seguir o canal de Loterias do g1 no WhatsApp

Além do grande vencedor, outros dois apostadores de Santa Catarina também foram premiados. Moradores de Concórdia e Riqueza acertaram a quina e cada um levou R$ 34.212,24.

No Brasil, outras 74 apostas também fizeram cinco acertos e levaram a mesma quantia. Outras 4.346 apostas acertaram quatro números, com prêmio de R$ 986,17.

Veja os números sorteados no concurso 3048 da Mega-Sena: 02 - 06 - 27 - 39 - 44 - 50.

Números sorteados no concurso 3048 da Mega-sena, em 23 de agosto de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/ Caixa

O g1 passou a transmitir, desde abril, todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

Acompanhe os sorteios no canal do g1 no YouTube

A Mega tem três sorteios semanais: às terças, quintas e domingos .

A aposta mínima custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet, até as 20h – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Os jogos podem ser realizados até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e o tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

Bilhetes da Mega-Sena, em imagem de arquivo — Foto: Marcelo Brandt/G1

articles.title: Google, Apple e mais: veja como é trabalhar nas empresas mais valiosas | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento com 1.750 grandes empresas dos EUA mostra quais gigantes oferecem melhores oportunidades de crescimento, estabilidade e início de carreira.
articles.summary: Levantamento com 1.750 grandes empresas dos EUA mostra quais gigantes oferecem melhores oportunidades de crescimento, estabilidade e início de carreira.
articles.body:
Estar entre as empresas mais valiosas do mundo não significa automaticamente ser o melhor lugar para construir uma carreira.

É o que mostra um estudo do Burning Glass Institute e da Schultz Family Foundation, que analisou a trajetória profissional de 12 milhões de trabalhadores em 1.750 grandes empresas dos Estados Unidos entre 2019 e 2024.

🗒️ Tem alguma sugestão de reportagem? Mande para o g1

O levantamento, chamado Where You Work Matters 2026, utilizou informações de plataformas como LinkedIn e Glassdoor para avaliar três fatores principais: as chances de promoção nos primeiros cinco anos de carreira, a retenção de funcionários e a remuneração oferecida.

A partir desses indicadores, o estudo concedeu selos às empresas mais bem avaliadas em diferentes categorias.

🏆 Overall Employer (Avaliação Geral): mede o desempenho da empresa considerando simultaneamente crescimento profissional, estabilidade e oportunidades de carreira.

📈 Growth (Crescimento): avalia as chances de promoção e progressão profissional dos funcionários.

🛡️ Stability (Estabilidade): mede a capacidade da empresa de reter trabalhadores por mais tempo.

🌱 Early Career (Início de Carreira): identifica as empresas que oferecem melhores oportunidades para profissionais nos primeiros anos de atuação.

Os resultados são classificados em dois níveis:

🏆 Platinum: grupo de elite do levantamento, que reúne as empresas com melhor desempenho em cada categoria.

🥇 Gold: empresas com desempenho acima da média, mas abaixo do grupo Platinum.

Para esta reportagem, o g1 fez um recorte das 10 empresas mais valiosas do mundo, segundo levantamento da Forbes. Oito delas aparecem no estudo: Nvidia, Apple, Alphabet (controladora do Google), Microsoft, Amazon, Broadcom, Meta e Tesla.

As empresas mais valiosas do mundo onde é melhor construir carreira

O resultado reforça uma das principais conclusões da pesquisa: o tamanho ou o prestígio da marca não são suficientes para explicar a qualidade da experiência profissional. O que faz diferença é a capacidade de oferecer oportunidades concretas de desenvolvimento ao longo do tempo.

Escritório do Google em São Paulo — Foto: Divulgação/Google

Abaixo, veja detalhes sobre a avaliação das empresas:

A Microsoft aparece como o principal destaque do grupo analisado. A empresa, conhecida por produtos como Windows, Office, Azure e Xbox, recebeu os seguintes reconhecimentos:

O conjunto de selos indica um desempenho equilibrado em praticamente todos os indicadores analisados, combinando oportunidades de crescimento, retenção de talentos e boas perspectivas para profissionais em início de carreira.

Além de controlar a maior plataforma de comércio eletrônico do mundo, a companhia é proprietária da AWS, uma das maiores empresas globais de computação em nuvem. A empresa recebeu:

O próprio levantamento aponta a Amazon como um dos exemplos mais bem-sucedidos na combinação de salários elevados, oportunidades de promoção e retenção de funcionários. Entre engenheiros de software, a companhia aparece entre os maiores destaques de todo o estudo.

Controlada pela Alphabet, a empresa é responsável por serviços como Google Search, YouTube, Android e Google Cloud. A companhia recebeu:

A Tesla, fabricante de veículos elétricos e tecnologias de energia limpa, ficou logo atrás das três líderes. A empresa conquistou:

O principal diferencial está nas oportunidades oferecidas para profissionais em início de carreira.

Fabricante do iPhone, iPad, Mac e de uma ampla gama de serviços digitais, a Apple recebeu os seguintes reconhecimentos:

Segundo os pesquisadores, os funcionários da Apple costumam receber bons salários e permanecem por mais tempo na companhia, mas as promoções acontecem com menos frequência quando comparadas às observadas em outras gigantes de tecnologia.

O caso mostra que uma empresa pode oferecer excelente estabilidade sem necessariamente liderar os indicadores de crescimento profissional.

Controladora de Facebook, Instagram e WhatsApp, a Meta recebeu:

A análise aponta que a retenção de funcionários é um dos principais pontos fortes da empresa. Por outro lado, os resultados ligados a promoções aparecem em níveis mais moderados, variando consideravelmente de acordo com a função exercida.

A Nvidia vive um dos momentos mais importantes de sua história e atualmente lidera o ranking global de valor de mercado graças à demanda por chips de inteligência artificial. No levantamento sobre carreira, recebeu:

A empresa se destaca principalmente pela combinação entre remuneração competitiva e estabilidade, características que ajudam a explicar sua reputação como empregadora em um setor marcado pela intensa disputa por talentos.

Ao mesmo tempo, trabalhar na companhia significa atuar em um ambiente extremamente competitivo e pressionado pela rápida expansão do mercado de IA.

A Broadcom, fabricante de semicondutores e softwares de infraestrutura, foi a única entre as gigantes analisadas que não recebeu nenhum selo corporativo geral . Ainda assim, isso não significa que seja necessariamente um lugar ruim para trabalhar.

O estudo mostra que diversas carreiras específicas receberam avaliações positivas, especialmente na categoria relacionada ao crescimento profissional. Entre os destaques estão:

Engenheiros de sistemas e segurança (Platinum)

Especialistas de suporte ao usuário (Platinum)

Além de comparar grandes empresas, o levantamento chama atenção para um aspecto frequentemente ignorado por candidatos e profissionais: a diferença entre salário, crescimento e estabilidade.

Segundo os pesquisadores, algumas empresas conseguem atrair trabalhadores oferecendo remunerações elevadas, mas apresentam resultados mais fracos em promoções e retenção . A Goldman Sachs e a Deloitte foram citadas como exemplos desse fenômeno em diversas funções técnicas.

A pesquisa também constatou que existe uma diferença média de 81 pontos percentuais entre as funções com melhor e pior desempenho em promoção e retenção dentro das empresas analisadas .

Para os autores, isso significa que olhar apenas para o salário ou para o prestígio da marca pode esconder uma parte importante da história.

articles.title: In 1934, an Arizona father began gathering rejected objects and desert Stone; 11 years later, the salvage had become an 18-room castle for his daughter
articles.summary: US News: Discover the story behind Mystery Castle in Arizona, built by Boyce Luther Gulley from discarded materials as a tribute to his daughter Mary Lou. Explore its unique architecture and historical significance.
articles.body: In the foothills of Phoenixâs South Mountain, an extraordinary house was built from materials most people would have thrown away. Between the 1930s and 1945, Boyce Luther Gulley gathered desert stone, rejected bricks, old railway materials, telephone poles, automobile parts and other discarded objects to build an 18-room castle for his daughter, Mary Lou. He worked largely by hand, shaping an eccentric three-level home into the desert landscape without a conventional architectural plan. What began as a private project became one of Phoenixâs most unusual landmarks.Today known as Mystery Castle, the structure stands as a striking example of vernacular architecture and an early exercise in material reuse. The National Trust for Historic Preservation says Gulley built the castle without formal architectural or engineering training, combining local materials, folk-art influences and recycled objects. The building eventually became a nationally recognised attraction, but its story began with a father separated from his young daughter and a promise connected to the sandcastles they had built together.From Seattle to the Arizona desertGulley was a Seattle businessman who had some training in architectural engineering. In the late 1920s, after being diagnosed with tuberculosis, he left his family and travelled to Phoenix, where the dry climate was then considered beneficial for people suffering from the disease. He eventually settled near South Mountain, at a time when the foothills were far less developed than they are today.Mary Lou had enjoyed building sandcastles with her father. The idea of creating something permanent may have stayed with Gulley after he moved west. Over the following years, he began assembling a house from whatever materials he could obtain. The National Trust dated construction of Mystery Castle to about 1934â1945. Architectural historians, however, noted that Gulley had begun building on the site earlier, with the structure evolving gradually rather than following a conventional construction plan. The result was a sprawling house that followed the contours of the hillside rather than imposing a regular architectural grid.A house assembled from what others rejectedThe castleâs unusual appearance was not simply the result of cheap materials. Gulley made the discarded objects part of the building's design. Railroad components became structural or decorative elements, old bricks became architectural details, and stones were carefully arranged into walls, fireplaces, niches and platforms.Historical Archaeology has shown that reusing building materials is not exclusively a modern sustainability idea but has long existed within vernacular building traditions. Inside Mystery Castle, practicality and eccentricity frequently overlap. The 18 rooms include a chapel, a bar and a room known as Purgatory. The building contains 13 fireplaces and a network of stairways and unusual passages. Built-in furniture was incorporated directly into the masonry, while some windows and decorative features were made from salvaged materials.The result was a building in which almost every feature carried a story about its previous life. Materials that might otherwise have been overlooked or discarded were given new functions within the castle, making the structure as much a collection of reused objects as a home. Its unconventional construction also reflected Gulleyâs determination to build according to his own ideas, without following the standard plans or materials used in conventional houses.Mary Lou inherits the castleMary Lou was 22 when she learned that her father had left her the property. She and her mother, Frances, travelled to Arizona and moved into the castle. The castle soon acquired another identity. In 1948, LIFE magazine featured Mary Lou and the unusual house in a story that helped give it the name Mystery Castle. The attention drew curious visitors, and Mary Lou and her mother later began offering tours. For decades, Mary Lou became the property's principal keeper and public guide, sharing the story of the building with visitors.Mary Lou died in 2010 after living at the castle for many decades. Before her death, she established a foundation to help preserve the property. The structure later faced another challenge. After vandalism and break-ins, Mystery Castle closed to the public in 2023, and a subsequent assessment found that stabilisation, repairs and accessibility improvements would cost about $3.3 million.In 2024, the National Trust for Historic Preservation placed Mystery Castle on its list of Americaâs 11 Most Endangered Historic Places. The designation brought renewed attention to a building whose greatest strength and weakness are closely connected: it was built as a highly individual, handmade structure rather than a conventional one designed for easy maintenance. Rejected bricks, old metal, desert rock and salvaged household materials were given new purposes and assembled into something that could not have been produced from a standard building plan. What survived was not simply a house, but an intensely personal architectural landscape built piece by piece for a daughter who would spend much of her life caring for it.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A British metal detectorist thought he'd found a bull's nose ring; it was actually a Bronze Age gold bracelet, and then two more appeared
articles.summary: UK News: In late May, dozens of metal-detecting enthusiasts gathered near Carlisle, in northern England close to the Scottish border, for a rally that also ser.
articles.body: In late May, dozens of metal-detecting enthusiasts gathered near Carlisle, in northern England close to the Scottish border, for a rally that also served as a protest against a proposed electricity substation. Over 4 days, the group searched roughly 470 acres and uncovered hundreds of objects, including a Viking brooch and an 1817 coin bearing the likeness of King George III. Among them was 34-year-old Scottish gas engineer Andy Crammond, who picked up a gleaming gold object he initially mistook for a bull's nose ring. But the object's unusual shine and weight quickly made him suspect it was something much older and more valuable. His friend Alan Daniels came over to inspect the discovery, and the pair soon uncovered 2 more remarkably similar gold objects nearby, revealing an extraordinarily rare Bronze Age find. The discovery transformed an otherwise routine day of searching into an archaeological breakthrough, with specialists later identifying the objects as complete gold torcs dating back more than three millennia. This extraordinary discovery highlights how grassroots archaeological efforts can uncover invaluable historical treasures, potentially reshaping our understanding of ancient civilizations while simultaneously informing crucial modern land-use decisions.Why archaeologists consider 3 complete Bronze Age torcs exceptionally rareAccording to Smithsonian Magazine, the 3 gold objects are torcs dating to around 1100 BCE, placing them around the transition between Britain's Middle and Late Bronze Age. Archaeologist Jim Morris of the University of Lancashire described the discovery as spectacular, noting that surviving torcs from this period are often found as broken fragments rather than complete objects. Morris told BBC News that even finding a single intact torc is unusual, making the discovery of 3 complete examples together particularly significant. The objects have a combined weight of about 18.3 ounces and have been valued at more than $400,000, according to reporting by the Telegraph. The finds have been submitted for assessment under Britain's Treasure Act, which determines whether archaeologically significant discoveries become the property of the Crown and whether finders and landowners may receive a reward.What Bronze Age torcs reveal about wealth, status and ancient communitiesBronze Age torcs could be worn around the neck or wrist, but archaeologists still debate precisely what they represented. Some researchers interpret them as symbols of wealth, status or authority, while others have suggested that particular examples may have had communal, ceremonial or ritual significance. Their physical condition can also provide clues about how they were used. Some surviving torcs show evidence of wear, repair or modification, suggesting that certain objects may have been used for long periods rather than immediately buried.For Crammond and Daniels, however, the discovery was far beyond anything they had previously encountered. Daniels, who has been metal detecting with Crammond as a hobby for several years, told the Telegraph that the pair had never found anything comparable. The remarkable preservation of the objects is partly explained by gold itself. Unlike many metals, gold does not readily corrode or tarnish, allowing the torcs to retain their distinctive appearance after more than 3,000 years underground.How a protest against a power substation led to the Bronze Age discoveryThe discovery has an unusual modern connection: the land where the torcs were found is at the centre of opposition to a proposed electricity project. The site could eventually accommodate infrastructure associated with the Cross Border Connection, a major project intended to strengthen electricity transmission between Scotland and England. Local campaigners have raised concerns about the potential effects of the development on the landscape, wildlife and surrounding communities. Members of Lothian Relics Metal Detecting were invited to search the area as part of efforts to document its archaeological significance before development could take place. Nobody expected the survey to produce 3 complete Bronze Age gold torcs.The discovery has now added another layer to the debate over the site's future. Campaigners say the finds, alongside other archaeological discoveries in the area, demonstrate that the landscape could contain important evidence of Britain's past. For archaeologists, the significance extends beyond the monetary value of the gold. Three complete torcs buried together offer a rare opportunity to investigate Bronze Age craftsmanship, movement, wealth and ritual practices, potentially revealing details about a society that existed more than 3,000 years ago.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Andy Burnham refuses to rule out tax rises in autumn Budget
articles.summary: Experts have warned that he and Chancellor John Healey will have little room to manoeuvre in their first Budget.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has refused to rule out tax rises in the upcoming autumn Budget, saying he "won't be unrealistic" about the "challenging" state of public finances.

The prime minister said he would take a "careful approach" to the economy, and defended his previously announced cost of living pledges as funded spending commitments.

Burnham became prime minister in July promising to give people breathing space and help with the cost of living, but questions remain over how major policies such as social care reforms will be funded.

Experts have previously warned that he and Chancellor John Healey will have little financial room to manoeuvre in their first Budget on 28 October.

Speaking during his first visit to Ukraine , Burnham said the policies announced so far including capping bus fares at £2 and cutting VAT on household electricity bills were "the first steps that I've felt able to make", and were doable because he was able to reprioritise funding from elsewhere.

"I took the decision early on that digital ID wasn't the top priority for now. And so we've reprioritised funding to other priorities," he said in an interview with ITV.

Asked if the public needed to accept some of the new policies would have to be paid for in tax rises, Burnham said they wouldn't necessarily have to accept that.

Pushed on whether he would need to raise taxes to cover spending gaps, he said: "I will always take a careful approach to things. I ran Greater Manchester for 10 years and we ran a very tight ship with rock solid finances.

"Nothing will change as I come into this role as prime minister. I won't take risks with people's jobs or their livelihoods or their family finances.

"I will try to help them in whatever way I can, I have already done some things that will help them."

Burnham previously told the BBC he accepts his earlier announcements aimed at tackling the cost of living are not enough on their own and hinted at further support.

Speaking during his first official overseas visit on Monday, he said while he would do what he could, "I won't be unrealistic and people really need to understand that.

"We are in a challenging position, whatever I do will be carefully thought through, it will be funded and there will be more to come as we go into the autumn."

Last week official figures showed the the government borrowed more than expected in July , despite a record month for income tax receipts.

Inflation also reached a four-month high of 2.9% in July and is expected to rise further due to the ongoing impact of the Iran war, which has hit energy prices and fuel costs.

Experts have warned Burnham and Healey that they need to either raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere as pressure on the public finances has left no room for extra borrowing.

Both the prime minister and chancellor have vowed to stick to the fiscal rules set by former chancellor Rachel Reeves.

The rules are designed to ensure day-to-day spending is funded through tax revenue by the end of the Parliament, and to reduce debt as a proportion of GDP.

Rain Newton-Smith, chief executive of the Confederation of British Industry, said business owners wanted to create opportunities for young people but "the cost of employing people has gone up so much".

"The business leaders I speak to say that the cost of doing business has gone up so much that it's holding them back from creating opportunities," she told the Today programme.

She said targeted support for businesses would create "more growth and more opportunities that saves money for the government and ultimately leads to higher tax receipts".

Burnham warned Iran war could hit UK growth next year

articles.title: Kaixiao Liu: New Zealand religious sect leader jailed over death of elderly Chinese follower
articles.summary: The body of 70-year-old Shulai Wang was found near a marina in Auckland in 2024.
articles.body:
A New Zealand court has jailed a religious sect leader over the death of an elderly follower who had travelled from China to live with his family.

Kaixiao Liu was found guilty of manslaughter and kidnapping, and sentenced to more than 10 years in prison.

The body of 70-year-old Shulai Wang had been found wrapped in rice bags near Auckland's Gulf Harbour in March 2024, sparking a major homicide investigation which eventually led to Liu.

Liu, a musician who previously appeared in a talent show in China, had denied the charges. He also denied he is a cult leader and said he only attracted followers through his music.

During the trial the court heard that Wang had travelled from Hainan island in China to New Zealand in August 2023.

She moved in with Liu and his family at their house, which Liu had called "the Ark", along with several other female followers.

Prosecutors said that the women acted in "servitude" to Liu and his family, and their lives were tightly controlled by Liu, where they referred to him as "Lord" or "Master".

Wang reportedly spent her days taking care of Liu's children, studying scripture, and planting vegetables.

The court heard that Wang had struggled to comply with the strict rules, possibly due to her old age, and was frequently disciplined.

In March 2024, Wang tried to escape but was caught and restrained. She died later that day, the court heard.

The court heard that Liu, his family, and his followers dumped Wang's body near a marina at Gulf Harbour. Liu had taken his children along for the trip "as camouflage".

The body was found by a fisherman days later. Police eventually traced the rice bags used to wrap Wang's body to Liu, who had made unusually large purchases of that brand of rice.

Besides Liu, his wife, Lanyue Xiao, was sentenced to nearly eight years in jail for kidnapping and manslaughter, amongst other charges. His mother, Xiuyun Li and father, Jingui Liu, had earlier been convicted of kidnapping and misconduct to human remains and are due to be sentenced later this year.

On Tuesday's sentencing, Liu's lawyer asked for leniency arguing that his client feels remorse and "is not a cult leader, nor requires people to follow his cult", according to Radio New Zealand.

New Zealand media outlets reported that Liu had attended a military-based university in China.

In 2011, he was a contestant for China's Got Talent - clips posted online showed him singing onstage blindfolded.

Sometime in 2017, he moved to New Zealand along with Xiao, and the couple became permanent residents.

Liu attracted followers on Chinese social media where he posted religious discussions, video diaries, and clips of himself singing. He also set up a project called Universal Choir that produced cosmic-themed orchestral music.

During the trial a police officer who interviewed one of Liu's female followers gave testimony. He said in court that the woman told him she "met the people over the internet through a song website, and she referred to the occupants of the house as friends".

During the sentencing, Justice Mathew Downs said Liu had shown "callous indifference" towards Wang.

"Because of you, Ms Wang died a lonely, frightening death. You display no remorse whatsoever. You should feel shame."

articles.title: ED raids 8 locations in fake call centre case, Mohali premises linked to fraud
articles.summary: MOHALI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has conducted searches at eight locations in connection with a suspected fake call centre fraud and money lau.
articles.body: MOHALI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has conducted searches at eight locations in connection with a suspected fake call centre fraud and money laundering case, with sources indicating that a key premises linked to the alleged operation was located in Sector 108, Mohali.According to sources, the ED's Chandigarh Zonal Office carried out searches at premises associated with Vijay Raj Kapuria, Varinder Raj, M/s Infimum Enterprises LLP and other persons and entities allegedly linked to the case. The searches covered locations in Chandigarh, Mohali and Madhya Pradesh.Sources said the agency recovered around Rs 20 lakh in cash, besides digital devices and other material during the searches. articles.title: Food influencers v critics: Why credibility counts
articles.summary: People on the food scene look at the rise of influencers and the role of social media in the industry.
articles.body:
When stuck for ideas about where to eat on a Friday night or torn between takeaways, more and more people are turning to social media and their favourite content creators for inspiration.

Research by one Bristol food writer has raised questions about transparency, with some creators guaranteeing positive coverage in advance and offering not to make clear their review was in exchange for a free meal.

Those promises of good reviews were made before they had eaten a bite - or realised the restaurant they had been asked to promote did not exist.

So can diners trust influencers to give an honest opinion and what is their role in shaping where we eat? We asked people in the food scene to share their thoughts.

Strangers at festival help autistic man realise dream

Travellers' camp mess causes football club disruption

Cut cables leave shops unable to take card payments

Meg Houghton-Gilmour, food writer and founder of The Bristol Sauce, undertook a two-part research piece into the world of food influencing when she created a website and social media account for a fake Japanese restaurant "coming soon to Bristol".

She messaged 48 influencers asking how much they would charge to make content, what would guarantee positive coverage and whether they would declare it an advert.

After receiving 33 responses, she said the prices quoted by influencers varied widely. Some said they would post in exchange for free food and drink, without an extra payment on top - and five of those said they would post without labelling the content as an advert.

UK advertising rules state paid posts must be clearly marked with #ad or a platform's paid partnership feature. This includes free meals in exchange for posts.

Houghton-Gilmour added the requests she sent out had created a swell of "misleading" positive noise on social media around the upcoming opening.

"I realised how insular and repetitive it is. Everyone going to the same places, saying the same thing," she said.

With more than 135,000 followers on Instagram and millions of views on TikTok , Oscar Bostock, also known as Bos Finesse, is a driving force as a food creator in Bristol and said becoming an influencer was a "no-brainer".

"There are food creators in the social media space, like myself, who do have a lot of credibility. But we need to respect the culture a bit as well.

"You'll never beat the people that write about food for a living. I don't really like to review and criticise food - I'll leave that to the professionals.

"At the same time, you need people here like myself to just celebrate food," he adds.

Bostock says authenticity is very important to him, and told the BBC there are many places he has said no to reviewing or reflecting.

"It's worth explaining it, being paid for a restaurant to say, 'this is good' is completely different to being paid to promote a new menu or venue.

"I feel very strongly about it, anywhere I work with had to be a place I actually valued and would visit in my own time."

Food critic Jay Rayner, who writes for the Financial Times, believes his role is to write "as interesting, entertaining [and] truthful column" as he can.

"I don't think there's much truth in the idea that the newspaper critic is dead," he said. "What I see happening is an awful lot more media around restaurants, full stop.

"I know, anecdotally, that a good review from me still results in many bookings, which is lovely - but it's not actually a concern of mine."

He said people sometimes ask if influencers "pose a challenge to what you do".

"My response is, 'only if it's better than what I do'," said Rayner, stressing his authority as a critic is not unassailable. "I do not have a right to my lofty perch."

Rayner said newspapers such as the Financial Times would "pick up the bill" for critics writing reviews, whereas a lot of influencers were invited to eat for nothing, which is something consumers should be aware of.

"That does undermine the credibility of the review," he said. "[But] you know, we're all celebrating the culture of eating food and eating out."

Adam Armstrong, head chef at Bath's Emberwood, said the sort of promotion restaurants received from influencers was something the industry would have been "screaming out for" years ago.

"If you make a bit of noise here or there, it just puts you on the map," he said.

He acknowledged many people had a "negative" view of food creators, but added: "People give them too much reverence in the first place. They're just people with an opinion."

The Nook Cheltenham, in Gloucestershire, has worked hard at being Instagram-friendly, currently boasting more than 11,000 followers.

Director and founder Edward Surman said: "Social media is a place where brands can alter their own story - where it's not moved around by the press."

Surman maintains influencers are not replacing food critics, but more of an "augmentation".

Wiltshire-based food influencer Baljinder Kaur Sangha-Gill, also known as The Authentic Punjabee, says her pages have moved beyond a list of recommendations and have come to represent a community of friends.

"Influencers haven't replaced critics. We've just opened the conversation about food," she said.

"Years ago, when you were looking for a restaurant or recipe, you'd wait for the Sunday paper. Now you can just go onto TikTok."

But she cautions not everything on social media is reliable.

"People will get free things to promote something. You've got to be aware of that. I'm very careful with that, I don't lie to my followers," she added.

Following her research, Houghton-Gilmour added: "Influencers are a symptom of the society and tech world we live in - not the problem. It's the tech billionaires making it unclear what's an ad and what's not."

She said the problem was not people making content but the lack of transparency, although she accepted that was not true of all influencers.

articles.title: Blood Moon partial lunar eclipse: How and when to see it in UK skies
articles.summary: There will be a partial lunar eclipse in the UK on 28 August, and may cause the Moon appear reddish in colour.
articles.body:
Skywatchers across the UK could have the chance to see a stunning partial lunar eclipse later this week as the Sun, Earth, and Moon line up in the night sky.

Lunar eclipses occur when the Moon is full which will take place in the early hours of 28 August. It may cause the full Moon - nicknamed the Sturgeon Moon - to take on an eerie reddish glow.

It comes just weeks after the UK experienced its most dramatic partial solar eclipse in nearly 30 years.

Adding to the spectacle, its position in the sky will be low on the horizon, causing a phenomenon known as the Moon illusion. This makes the Moon appear bigger and more dramatic than usual.

How and when can I see the partial lunar eclipse in the UK?

The eclipse will take place in the early hours of Friday 28 August.

The partial eclipse will begin at 03:33 BST in London, when the Moon enters Earth's darkest shadow.

It will reach its maximum at 05:12 BST, when around 90% of the Moon will be within the umbra.

By this point the Moon will be very low in the south-western sky, causing something known as the Moon illusion .

This is a term for when the Moon appears much larger than it is based on its position in the sky - an effect caused by the way our brains process visual information.

The effect is particularly noticeable during a moonrise or moonset, when the lunar disc is seen alongside familiar objects on the ground.

Exact moonset times will vary across the UK.

In London, it will set and move out of sight at approximately 06:15 BST.

A lunar eclipse happens when the Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon, causing the Moon to temporarily move into the Earth's shadow.

During a partial eclipse, only part of the Moon enters the darkest section of that shadow, known as the umbra.

The Moon is not completely cut off from sunlight, however.

Sunlight passing through the Earth's atmosphere is scattered, with shorter blue wavelengths scattering more easily, while more of the longer wavelength red light reach the Moon.

These wavelengths are then reflected back towards Earth, giving the eclipsed Moon its reddish colour.

What is the weather forecast for the Blood Moon lunar eclipse?

For the best chance of seeing the eclipse, astronomers recommend finding a high location with an unobstructed view towards the south-western horizon.

Clear skies will, of course, be essential.

Viewing conditions are expected to vary considerably across the UK during the early hours of Friday morning.

With low pressure in charge, cloud and heavy showers are likely to affect some parts of the country, while other areas remain clear.

Currently, the best viewing conditions are expected across central and eastern parts of England and Wales. However, even here, the cloud cover could change a lot from one hour to the next and is very hard to forecast accurately.

You can check the latest hour-by-hour forecast where you are online or via the BBC Weather app.

articles.title: No longer safe at the rear? How Chinaâs hypersonic weapons could hunt US support aircraft
articles.summary: International News: China has developed hypersonic glide vehicles that can launch air-to-air missiles, a new capability that could threaten high-value US aircraft such as.
articles.body: China has developed hypersonic glide vehicles that can launch air-to-air missiles, a new capability that could threaten high-value US aircraft such as command-and-control and surveillance planes from thousands of miles away, according to Bloomberg.The development is part of Chinaâs wider effort to expand the use of its huge missile arsenal for different military missions. A person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that China has also added air-to-air capabilities to some hypersonic cruise missiles and anti-ship capabilities to several other missile types.Hypersonic weapons could target support aircraftUS military aircraft such as aerial tankers, airborne warning-and-control planes and flying command posts are designed to stay away from the main battlefield. But the new Chinese weapons could put even these aircraft at risk.A hypersonic glide vehicle launched by a DF-17 missile could travel about 1,500 miles (2,414 km), a distance just short of the route from China to the US territory of Guam, a major American military base.Chinaâs DF-27 missile has an estimated range of about 5,000 miles, putting Hawaii within its reach.Hypersonic glide vehicles, or HGVs, are warheads that can move and change direction while travelling through the atmosphere. This makes them harder to track and intercept than traditional ballistic missiles.No other country is publicly known to operate a weapon that combines an HGV with air-to-air missiles.A report by the US air forceâs China Aerospace Studies Institute this year said that Chinaâs missile modernisation efforts âincreasingly prioritize the ability to inflict coordinated, systemâlevel damage across an adversaryâs operational architecture.âWeapon has major challengesDespite the threat, using a ballistic missile to attack an aircraft thousands of miles away would not be simple.At maximum range, a ballistic missile could take 20 minutes or more to reach its target. This means the missile would need highly accurate and constantly updated information about the aircraftâs location.The process of collecting information from distant sensors and passing it to the missile creates a long âkill chainâ, which an enemy could potentially disrupt.There is another major risk. A ballistic missile launch could be mistaken for a nuclear attack. This âdiscrimination problemâ could make the weapon especially dangerous during a major conflict, as an opponent might misinterpret the launch and respond with nuclear weapons.China expands missile arsenalChina appears to have sharply increased missile production in recent years. Bloomberg reported in May that Chinese missile production rose at the fastest pace since Xi Jinping became president in 2013, based on its analysis of the sectorâs finances.Chinaâs long-range PL-15 air-to-air missile has already been used in combat. The missile featured during last yearâs brief conflict between India and Pakistan, with Pakistan saying it used the weapons to shoot down several Indian aircraft.The Pentagon estimated that China had at least 3,150 ballistic missiles and 300 ground-launched cruise missiles as of 2024. Those figures represented increases of 147% and 50%, respectively, from 2015, when the US began publicly disclosing such estimates.US also develops longer-range missilesLong-range air-to-air missiles are considered important for any future major conflict.The US has developed the AIM-174B from RTX Corp.âs SM-6 air defence missile. Its exact range is classified, although the ground-launched SM-6 can travel 250 miles or more.On Saturday, the US Navy said it was testing the AIM-424 Malice air-to-air missile made by RTX unit Raytheon Co. The missile has a range of more than 300 miles, according to the Navy.Lockheed Martin Corp.âs AIM-260 is also in production but has not yet entered service. It is expected to have a very long range.In Europe, MBDA Missile Systems Services SASâ Meteor is widely used. The ramjet-powered missile can strike targets more than 100 miles away.

The missile has a range of more than 300 miles, according to the Navy.Lockheed Martin Corp.âs AIM-260 is also in production but has not yet entered service. It is expected to have a very long range.In Europe, MBDA Missile Systems Services SASâ Meteor is widely used. The ramjet-powered missile can strike targets more than 100 miles away.

articles.title: Looking to improve your TV's picture quality? These 5 setting changes can help
articles.summary: Tech News News: Many people spend hours watching movies, shows and sports on their TV, but only a few make the most of their screenâs picture quality. The good news i.
articles.body: Many people spend hours watching movies, shows and sports on their TV, but only a few make the most of their screenâs picture quality. The good news is that users do not need expensive equipment or professional calibration to improve their TV picture. A few simple changes to picture mode, brightness, motion settings and sharpness can make movies, shows and sports look more natural and detailed. Here are some of the most important TV settings to change for better picture quality.Start with the right picture modeThe first setting to check is Picture Mode. Most TVs offer options such as Standard, Vivid, Dynamic, Sports, Movie, Cinema and Filmmaker Mode. These modes generally aim for a more accurate and natural-looking image. Filmmaker Mode, where available, also reduces extra picture processing. Vivid and Dynamic modes may look eye-catching, but they can push brightness and colours too far for regular viewing.Turn off motion smoothing for moviesIf movies look unusually smooth, almost like a soap opera or live television, motion smoothing could be the reason. This feature adds extra frames to make movement appear smoother.Motion processing can be useful in some situations, but many viewers prefer to switch it off or lower it when watching films. It might be called MotionFlow or Picture Clarity, depending on the brand of your TV.Carefully adjust brightness and contrastThe brightness and contrast can make a big difference to what you see on screen. Contrast affects highlights and bright areas, while brightness or black level setting affects how much detail is visible in dark scenes.A good approach is to use a familiar movie or show with both dark and bright scenes.Don't increase sharpness too muchMore sharpness does not always mean more detail in the picture quality. Instead, it can add artificial outlines around objects and make the image look unnatural. Hence, it is recommended to lower the sharpness setting. Having said that the best level can vary by TV and personal preference.Check energy-saving and automatic brightnessSome TVs automatically adjust screen brightness depending on the room lighting or energy-saving settings. While these features can help in reducing power consumption, they may also make the picture look dim.If the screen appears inconsistent, checking features such as ambient light sensors, adaptive brightness or energy-saving modes may help. Available settings and names differ between TV brands and models.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Apple says farewell to Tim Cook with OneRepublic, tributes from Steve Jobs' wife Laurene Powell Jobs, and a 'personal life update' from CEO himself after 12 years
articles.summary: Tech News News: Apple threw a farewell party for its outgoing chief at Apple Park on Sunday, spilling out of CaffÃ¨ Macs, the cafeteria tucked into the ring-shaped Cup.
articles.body: Apple threw a farewell party for its outgoing chief at Apple Park on Sunday, spilling out of CaffÃ¨ Macs, the cafeteria tucked into the ring-shaped Cupertino headquarters, and into the courtyard at its centre, where OneRepublic performed in the round. A photo on X shows Cook holding a guitar, standing with the band.About 200 people were there, almost all of them Apple employees, The Information reported. Somewhere in the evening, Cook did something he has done publicly only once before in his 15 years running the company. Speaking to the room, he acknowledged his partner and called him by his first name, Mike.Laurene Powell Jobs and Jeff Williams were among those who paid tributePowell Jobs, wife of Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, spoke at the event. So did Jeff Williams, the chief operating officer who retired last year, and Eddy Cue, who runs services and health. John Ternus, the hardware engineering boss taking over as Apple CEO next Tuesday, also offered remarks. There were no politicians and no celebrity parade, just a room made up almost entirely of colleagues.Tim Cook has kept his personal life off the record since coming out in 2014He came out in a Bloomberg Businessweek essay in October 2014, writing that being gay had given him "the skin of a rhinoceros", which he said came in handy in his job. He described the decision as a trade-off with his own privacy and said he did not consider himself an activist. In the twelve years since, he has spoken far more often about privacy as a principle than about himself.John Ternus becomes Apple CEO on September 1 as Cook moves to executive chairmanApple announced the handover in April. Ternus joined the product design team in 2001 and has spent almost his entire career at the company. Cook becomes executive chairman, a role Apple says will include engaging with policymakers around the world, and Arthur Levinson shifts from chairman to lead independent director.The Information also reports a smaller detail that tells you what Apple is going for here. Cook's executive assistant will work with Ternus from now on. On his final earnings call as CEO last month, Cook said the transition was going seamlessly.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: British man dies fighting for Russia in Ukraine, first UK national killed in war
articles.summary: UK News: A 33-year-old British man from Barnsley, South Yorkshire, has been killed while fighting for Russia in Ukraine, reportedly becoming the first UK natio.
articles.body: A 33-year-old British man from Barnsley, South Yorkshire, has been killed while fighting for Russia in Ukraine, reportedly becoming the first UK national to die while serving on Moscowâs side in the conflict.According to the BBC, Bradley Townsend was killed on June 10 in Ukraineâs eastern Donetsk region after a remote-controlled FPV drone attack during what was described as a âstorm operationâ.Townsend had travelled to Moscow in April and signed a contract to fight for the Russian military, according to reports. He had reportedly told his family he was travelling to Romania.The British fisherman was recruited online by pro-Russian fighters Aiden Minnis and Ben Stimson, who are believed to have been fighting for Russia in the occupied Donbas region.In a video shared online in April, Townsend described himself as a ânormal working-class lad from Yorkshireâ and spoke about his decision to fight for Russia.âI came with the idea that I probably wouldnât be able to go home,â he said, adding that he understood what could happen to him.Minnis later announced Townsendâs death on social media, using his callsign âBadgerâ. A Russia-linked account described him as a âwarrior in a holy warâ who had sacrificed his life for the cause.The BBC reported that Townsendâs death is believed to be the first of a British citizen fighting for Russia since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.The UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office said it was aware of reports that a British national had died in Ukraine and was in contact with his family. It also warned that its ability to provide consular assistance in such circumstances was severely limited.British nationals have previously died while fighting in the Ukraine war, but they were fighting on Ukraineâs side. Townsend is believed to be the first Briton killed while fighting for Russia.The UK government advises against all travel to Russia and warns that travelling to Ukraine to fight or assist those engaged in the conflict could constitute an offence under British law, potentially leading to prosecution on return.Townsendâs death comes amid continued heavy fighting in eastern Ukraine, where Russian forces have relied heavily on drone attacks and infantry assaults along the frontline.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: âIt was me, not minister Keerthanaâ: Malaysian woman Vinosha Ravi says viral video was misused to spread false narratives, files police complaint
articles.summary: CHENNAI: A Malaysian woman, identified as Vinosha Ravi, has come forward to clarify that she, and not Tamil Nadu industries minister S Keerthana, is t.
articles.body: CHENNAI: A Malaysian woman, identified as Vinosha Ravi, has come forward to clarify that she, and not Tamil Nadu industries minister S Keerthana, is the person seen in a viral video that sparked a political row over the minister's clothing choices.In a video posted on her Instagram account, Vinosha said she wanted to clear the confusion, stating plainly that the woman being questioned over her attire is not the minister but herself. She pointed out that those making the comparison were likely unfamiliar with the difference between her and Keerthana, since they were not Malaysian.Vinosha said she has since approached the Malaysian police and filed a complaint over the matter.She described being deeply hurt by the episode, explaining that she was simply getting out of her car on her way to work when someone recorded and circulated the clip without her knowledge.She said the reactions to the video had been mixed, with some offering support and others posting negative and critical comments, including screenshots taken to mock her further.She said the clip had been edited and misused to spread false narratives, but that she had not let it break her down, even though the possibility of the video going viral had worried her. Her family and friends, she said, had reassured her that she was not at fault and had nothing to be ashamed of.Vinosha also pushed back against comments suggesting she should dress more modestly, noting that her outfit was appropriate for her job in Malaysia and that people criticised her regardless of what she wore. She said she had not been named or referenced in the original video at all.Calling the episode emotionally exhausting, Vinosha said she was now stepping back from the controversy and would not be posting further updates on social media, while thanking those who had supported her and urging people to stop sharing the video.The controversy began after a video showing a woman getting out of a car went viral, with several social media posts drawing a comparison with Keerthana, the first-time TVK minister and Sivakasi MLA, due to a resemblance.Keerthana had slammed the posts targeting the woman over her clothes, calling it evidence of a "fragile, regressive mindset" and clarifying that she was not the woman in the video. She had also said, "even if it were, why should it matter?", questioning why a woman's clothes or appearance should be treated as matters for public trial, and had accused followers of a rival leader of resorting to misogyny after failing to challenge the TVK on policy or governance.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chennai | Silver Rate in Chennai | Bank Holidays in Chennai | Public Holidays in Chennai | Chennai AQI | Weather in Chennai | Petrol Price in Chennai | Diesel Price in Chennai | CNG Price in Chennai | LPG Price in ChennaiStay updated with the latest Chennai news. articles.title: US judge rejects Ghislaine Maxwell's 'frivolous' appeal against conviction
articles.summary: The former Jeffrey Epstein accomplice loses her latest effort to be released from prison.
articles.body:
Ghislaine Maxwell's latest bid to overturn her sex trafficking conviction has been rejected by a US judge, who dismissed her claims as "frivolous" and "meritless".

The 64-year-old is serving a 20-year prison sentence for her role in procuring girls for the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein after being found guilty in December 2021.

Maxwell had appealed against her five felony convictions, claiming her constitutional rights had been "violated in multiple respects".

But a New York judge flatly rejected the appeal, describing it as "lengthy and rambling".

Maxwell said Epstein-related documents released by the US Justice Department earlier this year supported her case that she had been wrongly convicted.

But the judge ruled that "far from exculpating her, it incriminates her or reinforces the correctness" of her conviction.

The judge also said her appeal "falls very far from the mark", adding: "Nearly all its claims are procedurally barred; the overwhelming testimonial and documentary evidence adduced at trial conclusively established her guilt; and her petition's claims are demonstrably meritless, and generally based on speculation, distortions, and/or outright falsehoods.

"There is no fact that Maxwell fairly puts in dispute that has any potential to disturb the outcome of her trial."

The judge warned Maxwell against making further appeals, saying it "would not be taken in good faith" by the court.

Maxwell was found guilty in 2021 of facilitating Epstein's abuse. Prosecutors said she recruited and groomed girls, some as young as 14, between 1994 and 2004, before they were abused by Epstein, who died in prison in 2019.

Maxwell appeared virtually before the US House Oversight Committee in February this year but refused to answer questions, invoking her right to remain silent as she pleaded the Fifth Amendment.

Republican House Oversight Committee chairman James Comer said the situation was "very disappointing", adding: "We had many questions to ask about the crimes she and Epstein committed, as well as questions about potential co-conspirators."

Maxwell has previously sought a pardon from US President Donald Trump.

When asked last October whether he would consider pardoning Maxwell, Trump said he "wouldn't consider it or not consider it", adding: "I don't know anything about it, so I will speak to the [Department of Justice]."

The US Senate last month passed a resolution declaring its opposition to a presidential pardon for Maxwell.
